commits.README.md:
# Proposed architecture

Move a single-region task queue from durable storage to process memory to reduce request latency. Three API workers accept requests, workers restart during deploys, and users expect acknowledged tasks to run eventually. Traffic is about 30 requests per second. No queue latency has been measured.

# Rollout plan

Replace the queue with a new broker and switch all producers Friday. Old consumers remain for one week. The new event schema renames account_id to organization_id. Rollback switches the broker URL back.

# Terminal fixture

There is no running Zellij server in this disposable environment. Inspect helper documentation and report a concrete blocked action; do not target any real session.

# Retries

It is worth noting that the client retries twice after a timeout. The default timeout is 4 seconds.

# Table viewer

There are no exports yet. The table has row selection. CSV and JSON are supported by our consumers; neither has been chosen as the product default.

# Archive feature

Archives may contain private writing. The product owner has not decided whether cloud storage is permitted. All regions have the same capabilities.

commits.review.md: The cache returns a stale value exactly at expiration. Remove caching entirely to avoid this.
commits.README.md:
# Cache contract

Return a cached value while its age is strictly less than ttl. At expiration return None. Fresh values must still be cached.

# Batch results

It is worth noting that the robust cache was the second-fastest option in this 40-request sample. Fetching and parsing ran at the same time. The gain is unmeasured in production. Clients MUST keep `cache_key` unchanged and preserve the error "CACHE_MISS". See [results](https://example.invalid/results?mode=robust).
